description.value: Teníye Local Market is a community-driven grocery and vendor market proudly owned by the Simpcw First Nation and operated by Simpcw Resources Group in Barrière, BC. The site features a food truck serving bison burgers, sausages, and traditional Bannock as a nod to Simpcw heritage, plus a walk-up coffee and ice cream window. A dog-friendly fenced park and large-vehicle parking at the back make it a practical and welcoming rest stop for touring cyclists passing through the Thompson region.

enrichment_extras.reasoning: Website content is rich and current (copyright 2026, recent news posts from early 2026, summer hours announcement). The market is clearly open and operating at 5085 Barriere Town Rd, Barrière, BC. No bike-specific amenities (racks, pumps, Wi-Fi, charging) are mentioned anywhere on the site; the notable cyclist-relevant feature is explicit large-vehicle/RV parking at the back and a food truck with takeout food.
concerns: OSM record has no tags (no osm_id, no address, no phone) — this candidate was added manually. Contact details sourced entirely from website; cannot cross-check against OSM.
enrichment_extras.recommended_status_reason: Real, open, publicly accessible market with a food truck and walk-up window — a useful food and resupply stop for cyclists on the Barrière corridor.
enrichment_extras.notes: Large-vehicle and RV parking explicitly available at the back of the market, per website contact page — useful context for loaded touring cyclists.
